Could you look at these, which would be A, B, C, and tell this Court if that was -- that's an accurate reflection of the communes and the settlements as you know them?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: I know all these settlements but the first of May, Prvi Maj, is only a local commune. The rest are purely Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The rest would be -- there was only one Muslim village, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: No there is not a single Muslim village here. Prvi Maj, is an urban local commune where the population was mixed. The rest are villages populated exclusively by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Can I show you the next document? Which would be P1706. Which is again the assembly of the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf, which -- these are minutes, and on the second page, you will see some names -- sorry. Now, on the first page, we have persons elected to the working Presidency and there are three names there. Have you got them, Ninkovic, Glisic, and Vidovic? Do you know any of these people?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who are they?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: I know Ninkovic, Glisic, Zeljko Vidovic, Milan Surutka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And over the page there are the names of the newly appointed assemblymen and there are 13 names there. Could you tell us who these people are and whether you know them?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: All of these are names of Serbs. Out of these I know Nedeljko Ninkovic, Nikola Kisin, Ilija Boroja, Ranko Boroja, Nikola Zagorac, Milan Surutka, Ratko Kisin, Nedeljko Jovetic, Zeljko Nenad, Vojko Ninkovic -- Gojko Ninkovic, sorry, Luka Budisa, who used to work with me, Zdravko Kisin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Basically they are all --

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: I know the others too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were all local Serbs from --

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: By sight. All of these are residents of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, P1707, exhibit, Your Honours, show some more names. Were they members of the Autonomous Region of Krajina and the deputies who represent this municipality are seven names there, and the usher is bringing you the document. Again, Witness, these are seven Serbs and people who you know?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: All of these, again, are people from Donji Vakuf and I know them except for this number 4, Miodrag, there is no last name so I don't know who that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Can I now show you document -- Exhibit P1713, Your Honours? This particular document is a military document of the 30th Partisan Division command and they are minutes of meeting with a representative of the municipality of Donji Vakuf and Bugojno. I'm going to refer you to a certain paragraph in the middle, Mr. Doslic, and I'll read it out. If you can follow it in your B/C/S, please? Where it is reported in the minutes where it says, "I wish to stress once again that the tasks of the JNA Yugoslav army in this region, which is the" -- are you with me, Mr. Doslic? Have you got that part? It's in the middle of the page. Gentlemen and comrades, and then the next.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, so it says, "I wish to stress once again the tasks of the JNA Yugoslav People's Army in this region or more precisely the tasks of the unit under my command. Their task is to ensure peace, prevent interethnic clashes put all military formations under our command and prevent the activities of all paramilitary formations. We all know that the situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina is like and that is one more reason why we are here. The situation at Kupres was intolerable, there were several armies and paramilitary formations there and they all sowed fear and terror." From your own observations on the ground, Mr. Doslic, would you say that that was an accurate reflection of what was in fact happening?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to tell me which date we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the -- the document is dated 14th April, 1992. Mr. Doslic, if I can clarify my question and make it easier for you, perhaps, would you agree that the military was there to prevent interethnic clashes, as is reflected in this document?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: No, no. That's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any interethnic clashes, to your own -- from our own observations of being there at that time?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Well, at the time we are talking about, in Kupres, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are talking about Gornji Vakuf, when they say that there were paramilitary formations and the army was there to quell Muslim rebellion against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: No, no, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over the page, the President of the Donji Vakuf says, fifth line from that, that we have not had a single case of looting. Was that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Are you talking now about Donji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm always talking about Donji Vakuf, unless I tell you otherwise.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Is this the month of April?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, there were, but very little, because the Muslim population was still in Donji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like to show you Exhibit P1714. Which is again the decision on the appointment and again we have eight names. Would you confirm that you know these people, please? These are members of the council of national defence of the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it the right document?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: No, it isn't, Your Honour, it's 1714. Sorry, usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: This one is not on my list either, Your Honour. So again that's another one that I don't have and haven't looked at.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'm very sorry for this, Your Honours. I thought I had passed this list but perhaps I had not taken such care with the numbers but again it's just a document with eight names, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I know these names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they are all Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes, all of them are Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving right along, Mr. Doslic, Exhibit P628, usher. It's again a military document of the 5th Corps command to the 2nd Military District command, and it's a regular combat report. Item number 3, on that document, where it alludes to the destruction of the bridge over the Vrbas River in Donji Vakuf and the deaths of several people have exceptionally disturbed the population of this town. Individual provocations are still occurring, especially in the areas of mixed nationality. This confirms the destruction of the bridge, does it not, Mr. Doslic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you say that individual provocations were occurring at that time in the Donji Vakuf, as it -- the document states?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: I cannot -- because when the bridge was blown up, all the Muslim people retreated to their homes, and in the streets and around town, strong police and military formations began to move about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were no individual provocations? I will now take you to document P898, Your Honours. I'll take you to the item number 1. Have you -- oh, sorry. I'll describe the document while the usher is putting it on the ELMO, Your Honour. It's a command, military document, command of the 30th Partisan division. It's a regular combat report. Where it confirms, does it not, at one, information about the enemy, forces of the blue and reserve police are being mobilised at Bugojno and Donji Vakuf. That is your knowledge of the forces on the ground, is it not, forces, the reserve police were present in Donji Vakuf? Would you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Well, they mobilised only the Serb men, and armed them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in number 3, of that document, if the usher can move it up, please, situation in the territory, Mr. Doslic, where it says, "Once again it confirms following the destruction of the bridge in Donji Vakuf, most of the town's inhabitants of Muslim nationality and many of Serbian nationality left and now there is practically nobody in charge of the town. Would that be an accurate reflection from your own observations?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say that it was true that nobody was in charge of the town?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then he goes on to say, representatives of the Serbian municipality did not establish any authority so that neither the municipality nor the post office, nor the bank, nor any other institutions are functioning.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: They did establish a government, but only they were represented in that government. There was not a single Muslim or Croat occupying a position of any importance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you call that that they were then in control of Donji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I want to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Doslic. I will now take to you Exhibit P1716, Your Honours, which again is a military document from the 5th Corps command to the 2nd Military District command. It's again a regular combat report. If you go to item 3 on the first page, Mr. Doslic, second line on the third, situation in the area. "There have been no armed clashes but acts of sabotage against private property continue causing fear, insecurity and alarm among civilians." Mr. Doslic, who was conducting these acts of sabotage?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: The Serbs were responsible for all of these sabotage actions because at this time we are talking about, since the bridge was blown up, they started establishing their own control, and arrests began all over the town and the villages, and people were taken into custody and imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then it would be fair to say, fear, insecurity and alarm amongst the civilians was being caused by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then he goes to say that the ill feeling and I'll read here. "The capture of three Serbs in Donji Vakuf in the Turbe area has caused ill feeling amongst the Serbs, particularly among the Serbian organs of government which have adopted a cynical attitude towards the Muslim population, which might have serious consequences." What comment would you have on that particular statement in this document?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: No. By no means. And I doubt that it is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What is? What is not true? Because there are two statements in this sentence. Let's take them separately. Mr. Doslic, please follow me. The first part of the statement says as follows: "The capture of three Serbs in Donji Vakuf, in the Turbe area has caused ill feeling amongst the Serbs, particularly amongst the Serbian organs of government." Do you agree with that? Was there -- do you recall the capture of three Serbs in Donji Vakuf, around about this time, which caused ill feeling amongst the Serbs, particularly the Serbian organs of government? Do you know what this part of the statement is talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understood what you said, but this is not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then the statement continues to say that because of this, "The Serbian organs of government have adopted a cynical attitude towards the Muslim population, which might have serious consequences." Will you agree that there was at some point in time a situation whereby --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why, according to you, did the Serbian organs of government adopt a cynical attitude towards the Muslim population if it were not due to the capture of the three Serbs? If they did adopt a cynical attitude towards the Muslim population, why did they do so? Did they have a particular reason for doing so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we all know that they had a great idea of creating this Greater Serbia, and that failed.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you Your Honour, for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say, the last sentence on that page, "The Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. bridge in Donji Vakuf has been repaired." Was that true, from your own observation of the bridge?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was repaired by military engineering units of the Serb forces so that their column of vehicles, tanks and the rest, could cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to show you now document P375, Your Honours. It's again a military document from the 5th Corps command to the command of the 2nd Military District, and it's a regular combat report. I shall pause here for the usher to find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The usher has surely done her training for the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise to the usher, Your Honour, if I'm putting her out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at number 3, paragraph, situation on the ground, where it says there has been no armed conflicts in this territory, are you with me, Witness? Mr. Doslic are you following me? Yeah.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes, do I follow you. I told you already, since the bridge was blown up in Donji Vakuf, arrests began and people were taken away. The situation was bad. People locked themselves in their homes, and left the town in waves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So therefore you would agree that the situation was extremely tense, as this document reflects, and since the deadline for handing over illegally owned weapons has expired and the Banja Luka MUP Ministry of Interior, organs are making appropriate preparation to take away the weapons, people fear possible interethnic conflicts. Now, Mr. Doslic, it talks about weapons and a deadline for handing over these weapons. Can you comment on that? Was there such a deadline? And did indeed Muslims have weapons that they handed over?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: In Donji Vakuf, very few Muslims had weapons, and those who did were mainly huntsmen and they had turned over their weapons, but their main purpose was to have an excuse to come into somebody's home, look purportedly for weapons, and then take away whatever took their fancy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there anything for the Serbs to fear interethnic conflicts in the sense of the power balance between the Serbs and the Muslims, Mr. Doslic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Well, they were armed to their teeth, and people were afraid to resist. What could we do? We couldn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which takes me to Exhibit P640, which is another military document, usher. It's the 1st Krajina Corps command to the main staff of the Serbian Republic of BH Army, it's a regular combat report and I want to take you to paragraph 1, the second paragraph, where it says the situation on the part -- first page, Mr. Doslic. You're with me? "The situation on the part of the front south of the Sava River is still very complex. In the Prijedor and the Donji Vakuf area there have been cases of armed provocation and attacks by paramilitary formations." Would you think -- is that an accurate observation, from your own knowledge on the ground, that there have been armed provocations between the Muslims and the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: In Donji Vakuf, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would not consider that to be an accurate reflection of what you --

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: No, because the Muslims, for one had no weapons, and two, there were no provocations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the language says, in the Prijedor and Donji Vakuf area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I was coming to that myself actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There have been cases of armed provocations and attacks by paramilitary formations. No where does it say armed provocations between the Muslims and the Serbs as counsel put in her question. It doesn't contend that so how could he say that it's not accurate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, objection sustained. I would suggest, Madam that you rephrase your question. And also distinguish between Prijedor and Donji Vakuf asking of the witness whether he is in a position to report on any information that he might have with regard to the Prijedor or to the things happening, the events happening in Prijedor, because in Donji Vakuf, I would imagine that he's very capable of reporting to us but I'm not quite sure that he's in the same position as far as Prijedor is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Doslic, I refer to the Donji Vakuf area when I talk about when the sentence talks about the Prijedor and Donji Vakuf, can you please just concentrate on the Donji Vakuf area and it says there have been cases of armed provocation. Would you agree that there was armed provocation in Donji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: No. There was no -- none, and I meant precisely Donji Vakuf because I can't comment on what went on in Prijedor, since I was far away from that place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, still the question has nothing to do with what the report says. The report is dealing with the Donji Vakuf area, and we know in the Donji Vakuf area, there were armed conflicts going on between Croat and Serb forces, and she keeps changing what the -- learned counsel keeps changing what it says to suit her question. It doesn't say Donji Vakuf. It says the Donji Vakuf area. Which is a wider area than just the village itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, point taken again, Mr. Ackerman. Let me put the question. The report that you have been asked to look at Mr. Doslic, in this particular part, does not refer to Donji Vakuf, the town, or the village or the town itself. But it refers to the Donji Vakuf area, whatever that means. But I do have a map in front of me here, before me, and it seems to include large number of small villages. The point that has been made, and which is being submitted to you, is, to your knowledge, referring back with your memory to the events happening, not in Donji Vakuf town but in the Donji Vakuf area, if you are in a position to tell us, would you confirm the rest of the statement as it appears in this report, namely that there have been cases of armed provocation and attacks by military formations? Either or, or both?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean between Muslims and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Between anyone. The statement does not -- the report here does not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does not mention -- it just mentions that there were cases of armed provocation. Are you aware of any cases of armed provocation around about this time, preceding this report, in the Donji Vakuf area? Cases of armed provocation that you were aware of then? Or that you came to know about later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. If you allow me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the bridge was blown up, during those days and on, they entered houses, started arresting people, taking them away, so the population was intimidated. There were no conflicts whatsoever. The only conflicts that there were were caused by them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And one other thing: Are you aware of any attacks by paramilitary formations around about that time, in the Donji Vakuf area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean the town?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. In the area. Including the town. But in the Donji Vakuf area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When I asked you about armed provocation, who did you have in mind? What did you understand that I was asking from you? Armed provocation from whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Armed provocations in Donji Vakuf were caused by Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And were there any paramilitary formations, Serb paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those were indeed Serb paramilitary formations. That wasn't the regular police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So if this particular sentence in this report was referring to cases of armed provocation by Serbs and attacks by Serb paramilitary formations, in the Donji Vakuf area, would you agree with that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if instead it said that there have been cases of armed provocation by Croats and attacks by Croat paramilitary formations in the Donji Vakuf area around about that time, would you accept it as a correct statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I put to you the same question. If it referred to cases of armed provocation by Muslims and attacks by Muslim paramilitary formations in the Donji Vakuf area around about that time, would you accept it as a correct statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would like now the witness to be shown Exhibit P1721, please. This is the Crisis Staff of the Donji Vakuf municipality. It's a decision establishing the administrative organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Doslic, if you look at that decision, which the usher is now showing you, the council establishes the administrative organ under item 2 and it gives us eight names. Would you tell us whether you recognise these names and you know these people and who were they, please?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: I know Rajko Kisin, Ljubomir Kisin, I know him too. And Mile Ilic. As well as Milan Surutka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were all what ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: They were all Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Exhibit P1725, Your Honours, which is the Crisis Staff in Banja Luka, and the -- after item 7, just below item 7, you have Nikola Kisin, deputy in the Serbian Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina shall be appointed commissioner responsible for forming civilian organs of government in the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf, and it goes on to say that they are going to form the constitution, the Serbian Republic of BH. This name and this person is familiar to you, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was the one present at your exchange, the same person?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to show you Exhibit P1735. It's the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Ministry of Internal Affairs, from the public security station, and it's basically a list of arrested persons held in Donji Vakuf police security station from 27th of May to 12th of July, 1992. Do you have the list before you? Yes. Can you look on page 2 and number 48, would you see that name? Number 48?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: 48 is where my name is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. Now could you look at the other people? I believe you have looked at this document before?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you confirm that you have seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: This document? No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you look at the names and do you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Many of them. Camil Hadzic, Milan Petrovic, Hamdija Kuric, Safet Smajic, Tahir Smajic, Mulo Robovic, Uzeir Verem, Niko Barisic, Muhamed Smajic, Nasko Doslic, Dzevad Doslic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop. We don't need to go through all the list. Just a question: Do you recognise the majority of them? Do you know the majority of them? Yes, and then of course, madam, if you need to refer him to anyone in particular, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: No, that's fine, I just wanted to confirm that he recognised the names. Exhibit P1750 is a Reuters report, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Doslic, do you remember I showed this document to you at proofing?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you could go through this report, and if I would like -- I would like the witness thereafter to confirm that this is an accurate description of the Donji Vakuf at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The body of the document reads: "The mosques in Donji Vakuf where Muslims had lived in harmony with their Serbian neighbours for generations are now empty or destroyed. The town and its surrounding villages have seen their 11.000 Muslims dwindle to only 50 and half of those want to leave, said the President of the local council Nedeljko Ninkovic. As in hundreds of similar places across former Yugoslavia, this town just a few kilometres from the front line in Bosnia's bloody civil war has been hit by ethnic cleansing ripping communities apart. Asked whether the latest cease-fire, the 7th in Bosnia's civil war was being respected, the local Serb military commander said not one single cease-fire has been respected in this area, including this one." Your Honour, it goes on to talk about the people, the town, the lack of -- the shortages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Doslic, have you now had a chance to look at it? Would you confirm that this would be an accurate reporting of the situation on the ground in the town of Donji Vakuf as you yourself saw it?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Especially this first sentence, ending with Nedeljko Ninkovic's name. That's the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on page 2, it says, it all started on April 30, the Croats and Muslims from neighbouring towns sent us a lorry full of explosives hidden under a load of coal. What comment would you have to make on that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: I really don't know about that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It goes on to say it exploded in the centre of town devastating the bridge and over the Vrbas. Is your understanding that the bridge was destroyed by a lorry carrying coal?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes. The lorry was destroyed and you could see the coal traces. And also parts of a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's the last document, Your Honour. P1759 is a register of persons detained. Page -- sorry. Page 8, usher, if you could point him to page 8, item number 37, Mr. Doslic, once you have the document. Do you see item number 37, 16th June, 1992, it says first name and last name of the person, Dzevad son of Zahid Doslic, 24th August, 1957, date of birth. Is that yourself, sir?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The name of the organ who ordered -- decided the person to be brought in is SJB. And then the next column says, Mr. Doslic, reason for persons being brought in and detained and it says in your case, suspected of possession of weapons. As I believe is the case for all of them. Would you say that is true?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: No, no. As I've told you, when they wanted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The question is not precise. What is she asking is true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand it that it's whether he -- the suspicion of his possibly possessing weapons was true, was a founded one or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So the question is not whether he possessed weapons, but whether he knows whether or not he was suspected of possessing weapons? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When it says suspected of possession of weapons, do you think that was the ground under which you had been asked to report to the MUP and then you were subsequently arrested?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: I don't know how to reply to that question. They went into all houses and -- looking for weapons but taking other items. There were no weapons whatsoever in our house. I never had them. Nobody in my family had them. Then they would take the people away and imprison them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were you ever told why you were detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were you ever questioned in the course of your detention?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever asked by anybody that we have reason to believe you have weapons? Do you have weapons? Were such questions ever put to you at any time during your -- before and during your detention?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you think that this is an accurate reason for being detained that has been reflected in this document that you were suspected of possession of weapons or do you think there were some other reason you were arrested, and if so, what do you think that was?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: The other reason was that I was a Muslim. In fact, that was the main reason. And the second reason was that they wanted to break into people's homes under the pretext of looking for weapons and then carry out other items. I never ever in my life had any weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the rest of the list, if you have a quick look through, Mr. Doslic, there are some other names, and the reason given is exactly the same. Do you recognise the name firstly and I'll come to the reason second. If you just take a little time to look through the names I think you were shown this document by myself during proofing. Would you confirm that and that you had an opportunity to look at these names before?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: No. I have never seen this document before, but I recognise a lot of names here, and if needed, I can enumerate them. I can tell you which people I know. But their case is the same as mine. They would come to somebody's home, looking for a pretext to arrest them, and ask for weapons, and then after that, they would arrest them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because, Mr. Doslic, when you were first -- you said that it was the Serbs who came to your house and told your wife and daughter that if you did not report to MUP, your whole family would come upon some sort of harm, at that time, did they say that we believe that Mr. Doslic is suspected of having weapons? Do you remember that being reported to you?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: No, no, they didn't say anything. It's just that when my sister came out, I didn't come out, but my sister came out and they told her that if I failed to report they would come and get the entire family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And weapons were never mentioned at that time, could you confirm that, please?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD DOSLIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, that concludes my examination-in-chief of this witness unless there is anything else that I could assist the Court Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Madam Chana. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour first thing is counsel I think probably inadvertently said for the record that if you look at this document the reasons given for detention in each case are the same. If we just look at it it's clear that that's not the case. There are -- a large number have that reason but there are other reasons too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your statement is correct, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: One of them has to do with theft, one has to do what stealing flour, one has to do with detained by an army unit. They don't all say the same. Second thing, Your Honour, I was given to understand yesterday that the direct examination would take the entire morning. But it obviously moved much faster than they believed. I'm wondering if we might do this? I didn't have time during the last break to complete my communication with Mr. Brdjanin. I think another half hour might be very useful, and then that would enable us to maybe meet around 1.15 or something like that and I can report to you that situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you will conduct the cross-examination tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: First thing in the morning and I think it will be fairly short, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes and was it the understanding with the witness that he would be needed here tomorrow? Or arrangements have been made for his return?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: He's leaving on Friday so there is no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that is perfectly okay with us? All right? Yeah. Let's fix a time. It's half past 12.00 now, half past noon, now. 12.15?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: 1.15 Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1.15, my legal assistants will meet you as yesterday in the lobby and will escort you to my Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Actually it might be easier for him to meet in the Defence area, since we kind of go there anyhow. I can meet you at that stair landing just outside the Defence room area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just before 1.15. And Madam Richterova, please, if you could alert Ms. Sutherland as well, in case she has been in contact -- I don't know what is the arrangements between you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I can handle this by myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we will meet at 1.15 in my chambers. And here we are adjourning to tomorrow morning at 9.00 and we will meet to continue discussing the matters we were discussing in chambers yesterday which are strictly personal matters for the record, and are better dealt with in chambers rather than here in open court. Mr. Brdjanin will be briefed on these matters by your counsel. So 1.15, my chambers, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
